R1010.summary: Carpio to Fuenmayor: The French fleet has left Messina; rumoured bound for Brindisi, its design is to surprise Catania, and its good fortune makes any operation it undertakes to be feared. Carpio is dismayed by news from Brussels that the Prince of Orange raised the siege of Charleroi "intempestivamente".
R1010.en:
The French fleet has left Messina. It was rumoured to be heading to attack Brindisi in the Kingdom of Naples, but I
have now come to understand that the design is to surprise Catania; and given their great good fortune we must fear
the success of whatever operation they undertake.

I am left so confused and downcast by learning, from letters I have had from Brussels this week, that the Prince of
Orange has raised the siege of Charleroi out of season, that I confess to Your Lordship I lack the heart to speak of
so irregular an event and one of such pernicious consequences; nor do I wish to discuss it with Your Lordship, so as
not to add to the grief it will justly cause you.

R1011.summary: Carpio to Fuenmayor: After Charleroi, rumours that Spaniards were raising men by force for Sicily turned the Roman populace against them; Spaniards have been insulted and stoned in the streets for over fifteen days with no action from the Pope, while militia cavalry was brought in and guns added on Castel Sant'Angelo. Carpio contrasts the tolerance shown to the French, whose galleys pressed more than a hundred men, reapers included, at Civitavecchia.
R1011.en:
The Marqués de los Balbases writes to me that the effects of the siege of Charleroi are already felt at Nijmegen. But
that is no wonder, when at this court they make themselves felt with less reason, though to our greater surprise. As
soon as the news arrived, those ill-disposed to Spain spread the rumour that we were raising men here by force for
Sicily, and having [thereby] got the populace stirred up against our nation, they have insulted various Spaniards in
the streets these days. And although I have proved these rumours false, and the Pope and his ministers are not
unaware of it, I have not been able to obtain justice or satisfaction: not only is there [?no move] to punish the
seditious, there is [none] to find out the truth either.

R1009.summary: Carpio to Fuenmayor: False rumours are spread against the Spaniards; Carpio pressed the Pope for remedy and got neither remedy nor an inquiry, and has referred the matter to the viceroy of Naples and the governor of Milan.
R1009.en:
⟨I go on to tell Your Lordship that last week I reported⟩ what was happening at this court over the false rumours
raised against the Spaniards and fomented by our enemies. I can now only add that, although their groundlessness
has been proved, and although I have kept up with His Holiness the humble and urgent representations for a remedy to
such disorders, not only has no [remedy] been applied and no satisfaction given me, but I have not even been able to
get a single step taken towards finding out the truth, which only gives the populace more boldness against the
King's subjects. So, after several discussions and conferences with these cardinals of the party, it finally seemed
best to report, as I have done, to the viceroy of Naples and the governor of Milan on the state of the matter, and I
am awaiting their answers for my guidance.

R1006.summary: Carpio to Fuenmayor: The Pope and his ministers still give no satisfaction for the offences to the Spanish nation; Carpio awaits the governor of Milan's advice before a final resolution with the cardinals of the party. The French fleet and galleys, after keeping station off Catania, are said to have turned back towards [?Toulon] and [?Hyères], the galleys badly knocked about.
R1006.en:
⟨I have informed Your Lordship of⟩ the offences our nation has received at this court. To that I can now add only
that, as the Pope and his ministers persist in giving no satisfaction, I am awaiting the advice I have asked on this
matter of the governor of Milan, so as to take, with his advice and that of these cardinals of our party, the final
resolution that best serves His Majesty. The French fleet and galleys, after keeping station for some time off
Catania and its coast, are said to have turned back towards [?Toulon] and [?Hyères], and the galleys very badly
knocked about.

R1007.summary: Carpio to Fuenmayor: Still no satisfaction; on the cardinals' advice he stays away from papal audiences, awaiting the viceroy of Naples' answer.
R1007.en:
⟨In my previous letters I informed Your Lordship of⟩ the offences our nation has received [?at] this [court]. I will now
add only that this government still holds out without giving the satisfaction so justly owed to us, although [for my
part] I have pressed with the most urgent representations that the justice on my side [?calls for]. I have not gone so
far as to take a resolution, as I am waiting for an answer from the viceroy of Naples, to whom I have written on this;
meanwhile, on the advice of these cardinals of the party, I keep away from His Holiness's audiences.

R1008.summary: Carpio to Fuenmayor: No news at this court; he stands firm and awaits orders on how to proceed.
R1008.en:
⟨In the pending difficulties⟩ of this court there is nothing new: the government stands firm in its view, and I have
resolved not to move until His Majesty's orders [?reach] me, so as to carry out whatever he is pleased to decide.

R1004.summary: Carpio to Fuenmayor: Carpio laments Spain's ill fortune: the Cardinal d'Estrées's arrival at Turin threatens some novelty in Italy and Flanders is in the state Fuenmayor knows; the Congress must wait on the Prince of Orange's meeting with the King of England; the King's orders have not yet come. DECODE lists it as not decrypted; a faint margin decipherment agrees with the key.
R1004.en:
[and at the same time I must] lament with Your Lordship how our ill fortune pursues us everywhere: with the arrival
of the Cardinal d'Estrées at Turin some great upheaval is feared in Italy, and the affairs of [Flanders] are in the
state Your Lordship knows. As for the business of the Congress, it seems we must suspend judgement until we see what
comes of the meeting of the Prince of Orange with the King of England. On the difficulties at this court I have
nothing to add to what I told Your Lordship in my previous letters, except that, although I expected His Majesty's
orders by this post, I have not received them; but I do not doubt the next will bring them, for they write to me
from Madrid that the letters in which I gave the first reports on these affairs had arrived there.

R1005.summary: Carpio to Fuenmayor: The signs that the next campaign will bring war in Milan cause great concern, the Cardinal d'Estrées at Turin not being idle. DECODE lists it as not decrypted; a faint margin decipherment agrees with the key.
R1005.en:
besides which, the signs and plain indications that next campaign there will be war in Milan keep us very
anxious, for the Cardinal d'Estrées, who is at Turin, is not idle.

R1002.summary: Carpio to Fuenmayor: On the King's orders he asked Innocent XI for an audience on the pending disputes; the Pope refused it twice and would receive the King's business only through a cardinal, so Carpio declines to treat the principal business until the point is settled.
R1002.en:
On the pending affairs of this court, the King our lord, whom God preserve, is pleased [?to order me to] ask His
Holiness for an audience and tell him what his despatch contains about the satisfaction His Majesty is to expect for
what happened here. Having asked for the audience on Tuesday the 30th, His Beatitude was pleased to answer that he
could not receive me. Going back the next day, the 1st of this month, to beg His Holiness, through my maestro di
camera, to grant me the audience, since His Majesty orders me most strictly to [?speak] to His Beatitude in person on
the business he entrusted to me (for without so pressing an order I would not trouble His Holiness), His Beatitude
answered the same as the day before, without giving to understand the reason for the refusal, and added that if I
had business of the King's to treat, I should communicate it through some Cardinal.

R1003.summary: Carpio to Fuenmayor: The loss of Freiburg may change the plan of the winter quarters, the Duke of Lorraine having to recross the Rhine, and leaves Flanders in a miserable state. He recalls the Pope's two refusals of audience already reported, has not asked again, and awaits the advice of the Marqués de los Vélez, viceroy of Naples.
R1003.en:
The news of the siege of Freiburg is now very painful, for its pernicious consequences, since this mishap must bring a
change in the plan of the winter quarters, the Duke of Lorraine having to recross the Rhine; but I [leave] to Your
Lordship's consideration the miserable state in which Flanders is left.

⟨By the previous post I informed Your Lordship⟩ how His Majesty's resolution on the affairs pending at this court
had reached me, and that, having asked His Holiness twice for an audience, he had refused it both times in the
manner I reported to Your Lordship. As I have not asked for it again since then, there is no news to pass on to Your
Lordship: I am waiting for the answer to the advice I asked of the Marqués de los Vélez, which has not yet arrived,
and I have taken no step in the matter.

system: Point-separated syllabic nomenclator: numbers 9-30 single letters, 31-60 consonant-vowel syllables in rows of five, struck numbers a second syllable table, letter pairs as syllables with the consonant disguised, about twenty three-letter code words, struck…
